draft.title: Reading economic graphs
card: Line graph
A line graph shows how something changes over time. Time runs along the bottom axis, so you can see a rise, a fall or a steady trend.
Bar graph
A bar graph compares amounts across different groups or categories. A taller bar means a larger amount.
Supply and demand

A supply and demand model shows how price and quantity affect each other. The demand line slopes down: a higher price means buyers want less. The supply line slopes up: a higher price means sellers offer more.
Before you read a graph, check the title, the labels on both axes and the units. Then pick the graph that suits the question you are asking.

1.alt: A line graph of the price of a loaf of bread in a town from 2019 to 2023. The price rises from 3 dollars in 2019 to 5 dollars in 2023.

2.alt: A bar graph of money spent by four students in a week. Ali spent 12 dollars, Bella 20 dollars, Chen 8 dollars and Dana 15 dollars.

3.alt: A supply and demand model. Demand D slopes down and supply S slopes up. They cross at price P* and quantity Q*.

draft.remember: Line graphs show change over time, bar graphs compare amounts, and supply and demand show how price and quantity affect each other.

a.q: Which graph is best for showing how a shop's monthly sales changed over one year?
opts: A line graph, with months along the bottom
A bar graph, with one bar for each shop
A graph with no labels on its axes
a.why: Sales are changing over time, so a line graph with months on the bottom axis shows the trend. A bar graph with one bar for each shop compares different shops at one point, not change across a year.
a.clue: Which graph has time along the bottom?

b.q: A bar graph shows the number of tickets sold by four school fundraisers: Cake stall 40, Raffle 65, Car wash 30, Book sale 50. Which fundraiser sold the most?
b.why: A bar graph compares amounts, and the tallest bar is the largest. The raffle bar is the tallest, at 65 tickets. The book sale is second, at 50.

fig.alt: A bar graph of tickets sold: Cake stall 40, Raffle 65, Car wash 30, Book sale 50.

a.best: A line graph, with months along the bottom

problems.detail: The question text lists every value (Raffle 65, etc.), so students can find the answer by comparing numbers without reading the bar graph. It does not test the graph-reading skill the card teaches. Remove the numbers from the stem so students must read the chart.

check.summary: The card, graphs and question a are accurate. Question b states all the values in its text, so students can answer without reading the bar graph; the numbers should be removed from the stem.

flags: Question b, level: The question text lists every value (Raffle 65, etc.), so students can find the answer by comparing numbers without reading the bar graph. It does not test the graph-reading skill the card teaches. Remove the numbers from the stem so students must read the chart.
